subject: Reception and display joinery
hook: Big desk, narrow corridor. Here's how it gets in.
ig:
Big desk, narrow corridor. This is how commercial joinery gets into buildings that weren't designed for it.

A long reception counter or display wall rarely fits through a standard door in one piece. So the access route is part of the design, not an afterthought.

How we work:
Measure the way in: doors, corridors, stairs, lift.
Cut and edge every panel in our own workshop.
Assemble in sections sized to that route, and check each one for square.
Wrap, load and deliver with our own team.
Join the sections on site, level the run and fit the top.

You get one continuous piece of furniture in the room, without anyone discovering on install day that it won't go round the corner.

Planning reception or display joinery for your premises? Comment RECEPTION and we'll send the link.
fb:
One of the most common worries we hear from businesses: "Will it even fit through the door?"

This clip shows how we handle it. We measure the route in first, then cut, edge and build the furniture in sections in our Hanley workshop, each one sized to get through your doors, corridors or lift. Our team delivers it, joins it on site and finishes it as one piece.

It's how we approach reception desks, display units and storage walls for offices, shops and clinics around Stoke-on-Trent.

Got a space you're not sure about? Have a look at our cabinet making and get in touch.
